meta.notes: Battery Active Material Production (Europe) as of February 2026. Source: Battery-News.com / FEM RWTH Aachen University. All capacities in tonnes per year (t/a). pCAM = Precursor cathode active material, CAM = Cathode active material, AAM = Anode active material. Chemistry codes: SG = Synthetic graphite, NG = Natural graphite, NMC = Nickel Manganese Cobalt, LFP = Lithium Iron Phosphate, LNMO = Lithium Nickel Manganese Oxide, NCA = Nickel Cobalt Aluminum, Si = Silicon.

companies.name: Vianode
companies.notes: Vianode is a Hydro spin-off producing synthetic graphite anode materials.

research.summary: Vianode (Hydro spin-off) inaugurated Via ONE at Herøya in 2024 — the world's first large-scale low-carbon synthetic graphite anode plant, with a rated capacity of 2,000 t/a when fully ramped up (enough for ~30,000 EVs/yr). Vianode has a phased multi-billion USD expansion plan targeting ~60,000 t/a at Herøya and is also developing a facility in Ontario, Canada, with a long-term ambition to supply materials for 3 million EVs/yr by 2030. Plant is operational and ramping.

open_questions: Morrow is primarily a cell manufacturer — verify whether CAM production is a planned integrated facility or a separate entity

research.summary: Morrow Batteries ASA filed for bankruptcy on 6 May 2026 and all 210 employees were laid off. The company had planned to produce CAM (LFP/LNMO) in Mo i Rana as an integrated facility tied to its cell gigafactory — not as a standalone separate entity. With the bankruptcy of the parent company, the CAM plant project is effectively cancelled. The collapse was driven by cost overruns, delays in industrialisation, low battery market prices, and inability to raise further capital.

open_questions: Monitor Rotterdam mixing facility completion and qualification progress with battery makers

research.summary: CarbonX (TU Delft spin-off, 2014) is developing synthetic graphite anode materials using proprietary emulsion feedstock technology. Currently at pilot/pre-commercial stage — building a high-capacity feedstock mixing facility in the Port of Rotterdam. Raised €4M in 2024; in advanced qualification stages with major battery makers. 20,000 t/a production lines under feasibility study for Europe and US. No commercial production yet.

companies.name: E-Magy
companies.notes: E-Magy is a Dutch startup producing nano-porous silicon anode materials.

research.summary: E-Magy (Broek op Langedijk, Netherlands) produces nano-porous silicon anode material at an industrial pilot facility running 24/7, with current capacity reported at ~25 t/a. Plans call for scaling to 50 t/a by 2028 as a first commercial step. The company raised €20.5M from Hydro, Invest-NL and others and is active in qualification programmes with battery manufacturers. Long-term target is 3,000 t/a at a full-scale site. Note: the source image figure of 300 t/a has not been confirmed by company sources — reported pilot capacity is 25 t/a.

companies.name: Altilium

open_questions: Image reads 'allium' — assumed to be Altilium. Verify company name.

companies.notes: Altilium focuses on recycled cathode materials (closed-loop from black mass).

research.summary: Altilium (UK) recovers critical minerals from end-of-life EV batteries and manufacturing scrap and converts them into pCAM and CAM using its proprietary EcoCathode™ process. The planned ACT4 facility in Teesside would be one of the largest EV battery recycling and CAM plants in Europe, targeting 30,000 t/a CAM capacity — enough to meet ~20% of UK demand by 2030. A first pilot plant commenced operations in Plymouth in 2025; Teesside commissioning is planned for late 2027. Altilium secured £18.5M in funding in April 2026. Company name confirmed (not 'allium').

open_questions: Capacity not disclosed in source image — research actual production volume

companies.notes: Prayon is a Belgian phosphate chemistry specialist producing LFP cathode materials.

research.summary: Prayon (Engis, Belgium) is a fully integrated phosphate producer that manufactures LFP cathode material using its proprietary MGA phosphoric acid technology. Prayon operates a JV with Chinese cathode producer Pulead for LFP production, and supplies purified phosphoric acid (PPA) as feedstock for LFP. Specific production capacity at Engis in t/a is not publicly disclosed. Prayon is active as a licensor and technology partner for LFP supply chains in North America and Europe.

open_questions: Image reads 'orena' — assumed to be Orano (French nuclear/materials group). Verify.

research.summary: The Neomat CAM plant in Dunkirk is a JV between XTC New Energy (51%) and Orano (49%), operating under the name Neomat. Final investment decision was taken on 4 March 2026; plant operations are now targeted for 2028 (not 2027 as previously recorded). Planned capacity is 40,000 t/a NMC CAM, expandable to 80,000 t/a. Total investment ~€1.5 billion; ~1,300 direct jobs. A companion Neomat pCAM facility is also planned on the same Dunkirk site.

companies.name: Axens
companies.notes: Axens is an IFP Energies nouvelles subsidiary producing cathode active materials.

research.summary: Axens (IFP Energies nouvelles subsidiary) is building a CAM plant in Saint-Saulve (MACARON project) via a JV called LICAMAX. Planned capacity is 28,000 t/a NMC cathode material across four independent production lines; operations targeted for 2028. Total investment ~€500M; recruitment starts 2026. The plant is not yet operational — the source image figure of 25,000 t/a current capacity is incorrect; this is a planned facility. Status corrected to Planned.

open_questions: Battery-grade silicon output not yet at commercial scale — monitor R&D-to-pilot conversion

research.summary: Ferroglobe operates an established silicon metal plant at Sabón (Arteixo, A Coruña) since 1972, currently at commercial scale for silicon metal. Battery-specific application — high-purity silicon for Li-ion anodes — is in R&D/pilot phase following €2M investment in 2021–2022. Not yet producing battery-grade material at commercial volumes.

companies.name: Hunan Yuneng

open_questions: Monitor Phase 1 production start — construction permit granted, building underway

companies.notes: Hunan Yuneng is a major Chinese LFP cathode material producer with announced European ambitions.

research.summary: Hunan Yuneng (major Chinese LFP cathode maker) received a building permit and has begun construction of a 50,000 t/a LFP cathode plant at the ExpacioMérida industrial park in Mérida, Extremadura, Spain. Phase 1 investment ~€125M; total planned investment €800M with expansion to 300,000 t/a. ~500 jobs. Construction confirmed underway as of early 2026.

open_questions: Project scrapped Dec 2024 — monitor if Putailai revisits Europe after regulatory/market conditions change

research.summary: PTL (Putailai New Energy Technology, Shanghai) planned Europe's largest anode material factory in Sundsvall, Sweden — SEK 13B investment, 50,000 t/a initial phase expandable to 100,000 t/a. Project was scrapped in December 2024 after Swedish Strategic Products Inspectorate imposed regulatory conditions deemed unacceptable by the Chinese parent, compounded by Northvolt's collapse reducing demand outlook.

companies.name: Talga
companies.notes: Talga Group (Australian-listed) operates natural graphite deposits in northern Sweden and processes AAM in Luleå.

research.summary: Talga Group (ASX: TLG) is developing a fully integrated natural graphite anode project in northern Sweden: the Nunasvaara South mine and the Luleå Anode Refinery producing 19,500 t/a battery anode material (~250,000 EVs/yr). All permits are now legally final after Sweden dismissed all mine permit appeals in June 2025. Construction of the commercial refinery is expected to commence H2 2026, subject to final investment decision. The project has EU Innovation Fund grant (€70M) and EIB debt facility (€150M). An EVA pilot plant (50 t/a) has been producing since 2022. Planned target year 2026 in the database refers to initial small-scale supply from the EVA plant.

companies.name: BASF

open_questions: Capacity not disclosed in source image — research current pCAM output at Harjavalta

companies.notes: BASF produces pCAM at Harjavalta using nickel and cobalt refined on-site.

research.summary: BASF's pCAM plant in Harjavalta, Finland has faced a protracted permitting battle since 2020. In April 2024, BASF initiated change negotiations (potential layoffs) due to the lengthy and uncertain permit process. The environmental permit was upheld and became legally final in July 2024 (Vaasa Administrative Court ruling not appealed), but operations can only begin after a crystallizer is installed to handle sodium sulfate in wastewater. Capacity when operational: designed to supply ~400,000 EVs/yr with pCAM. Plant remains effectively paused as of mid-2026.

open_questions: Definitive Feasibility Study planned 2025 — monitor DFS outcome and GVA10 Phase 1 construction start; first production targeted 2027

research.summary: Grafintec Oy (owned by Beowulf Mining plc, UK-Swedish) is developing a Graphite Anode Materials Plant (GAMP) in Vaasa producing coated spherical graphite (CSPG) for battery anodes. JV with Epsilon Advanced Materials: Phase 1 (GVA10) targets 10,000 t/a, Phase 2 adds 40,000 t/a to reach 50,000 t/a. Full GAMP capacity 20,000 t/a CSPG. Definitive Feasibility Study planned 2025; first production targeted 2027.

open_questions: Verify company name — image reads 'Greyv' or similar. Confirm identity and current project status.

research.summary: No company named 'Greyv' could be identified in Finnish battery industry sources, company registries, or industry news as of May 2026. The name as read from the source image may be a misread — possible candidates in Vaasa with pCAM plans include Grafintec (NG AAM, separate record) or an unannounced project. The 34,000 t/a pCAM capacity figure and 2026 target year cannot be verified. Company identity and project status remain unconfirmed.

Umicore Finland Oy operates a pCAM (precursor cathode active material) production facility in Kokkola, home to one of Europe's largest cobalt refineries outside China. pCAM production with new NMC technology began in 2014; a second mass production line was inaugurated subsequently. Kokkola is a key node in Umicore's European CAM supply chain, producing NMC precursors for EV battery makers.

open_questions: CNGR Advanced Material withdrew from project — Finnish Minerals Group seeking new partner; monitor revival

research.summary: CNGR Finland Oy (JV: CNGR Advanced Material 70% + Finnish Minerals Group 30%) planned a 60,000 t/a pCAM plant in Hamina, Finland. Environmental permit was approved. However, CNGR Advanced Material withdrew from the project citing a challenging market environment. Finnish Minerals Group is seeking a new partner. Capacity was reported as 60,000 t/a (not 100,000 as initially logged — source image may have shown maximum expansion figure).

open_questions: Sample production targeted summer 2026; commercial production 2027 — monitor construction progress

research.summary: Easpring Finland New Materials Oy (JV: Beijing Easpring Material Technology 70% + Finnish Minerals Group 30%) is building Finland's first CAM plant in Kotka. Target capacity 60,000 t/a NMC/NCA cathode material (~500–800k EV equivalent/yr). Environmental permit granted; groundbreaking held; construction began spring 2025. Sample production targeted summer 2026, commercial production 2027.

open_questions: Identify company — logo not readable. 1,000 t/a SG AAM in Tallinn, Estonia, target 2027. Small scale suggests R&D or early pilot.

research.summary: The most likely match for this record is UP Catalyst (Tallinn, Estonia), a startup producing synthetic graphite from CO2 via molten salt electrotransformation (MSCC-ET). UP Catalyst has secured seed funding totalling ~€6.4M and is building an industrial pilot in Maardu (near Tallinn). Their industrial-scale unit targets ~27 t/a carbon materials (graphite + CNTs) from ~100 t CO2/yr by 2027 — consistent with the 1,000 t/a planned figure being aspirational/longer-term. Company identity not fully confirmed from source image logo.

companies.name: Topsoe
companies.notes: Topsoe (Haldor Topsoe) is a Danish catalysis company expanding into LNMO battery cathode materials.

research.summary: Topsoe inaugurated a 200 t/a LNMO industrialisation pilot in February 2024. Note: Topsoe's production site is in Frederikssund, Denmark — the source image may read 'Frederikshavn' in error; please verify the city. LNMO is a cobalt-free high-voltage (5V) spinel cathode; 200 t/a enables ~125 MWh/yr of battery cell qualification and small-series supply. Topsoe had a supply agreement with Morrow Batteries, which is now bankrupt; commercial scale-up timing is therefore under review.

companies.name: IBU-tec
companies.notes: IBU-tec Advanced Materials AG is a German specialty chemicals company producing LFP via flash calcination.

research.summary: IBU-tec's Weimar plant is producing LFP cathode material for automotive applications, with current capacity of ~3,000 t/a (slightly below the 4,000 t/a figure in the source image). IBU-tec signed a major supply contract with PowerCo (Volkswagen) for LFP material from 2026 onwards. A second, larger plant in Bitterfeld-Wolfen (15,000 t/a) is under construction, with the spray tower commissioning targeted Q4 2026 — this will be Europe's first large-scale LFP plant without Chinese technology. Weimar facility remains operational and in use during the Bitterfeld ramp-up.

open_questions: Preliminary feasibility study completed — monitor pilot plant construction start and production commissioning

research.summary: Altech Industries Germany (subsidiary of Altech Batteries Ltd, ASX) is developing a battery-grade graphite coating plant at the Schwarze Pumpe Industrial Park, Spremberg (Brandenburg). The facility uses Altech's proprietary alumina-coating technology to coat 10,000 t/a of anode-grade graphite for Li-ion batteries. Preliminary feasibility study completed; supported by Saxony state government.

companies.name: BASF
companies.notes: BASF CAM plant in Schwarzheide, Brandenburg — phase 1 capacity 10,000 t/a, producing NCA and NMC.

research.summary: BASF's Schwarzheide plant is the only fully automated large-scale CAM production facility in Europe, producing high-nickel NCA and NMC materials. Pre-commercial production began in 2023; capacity is targeting ~100,000 t/a (long-term), with a reported 20 GWh cell supply equivalent per year already sold out for coming years. BASF renewed a long-term CAM supply agreement for the Schwarzheide plant in September 2025 and signed a framework agreement with CATL in July 2025. The 10,000 t/a figure in the source image reflects early phase capacity.

E-Lyte Innovations GmbH opened Germany's first battery electrolyte production facility in Kaiserslautern in 2024, in partnership with FUCHS SE. Capacity: 20,000 t/a of electrolyte for Li-ion, Na-ion and supercapacitor applications. Plans to add another 20,000 t/a by 2026. Positioned as Europe's first industrial-scale, independent electrolyte producer.

open_questions: Production start earmarked early 2028 — monitor construction and permitting progress

research.summary: Pure Battery Technologies (PBT, founded 2017, HQ Brisbane, Australia) acquired the Königswarter & Ebell (K+E) facility in Hagen, Germany in 2020. The Hagen plant processes Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) and battery black mass into pCAM (precursor Cathode Active Material) using a low-CO2 hydrometallurgical process — up to 85% less CO2 than conventional methods. Current permitted capacity: 2,500 t Ni/yr; expanding to 15,000 t/a pCAM. Production start earmarked early 2028. EIB InvestEU-backed.

open_questions: Verify company full name and current project status — 'Ionway' as read from image

research.summary: Ionway is a JV between Umicore and Volkswagen Group's PowerCo, building a CAM (NMC) plant in Nysa, Poland, adjacent to Umicore's existing Nysa facility. Production start was targeted for 2026 with an initial annual supply capacity of ~40 GWh (equivalent to ~60,000 t/a NMC as per the source image). Long-term ambition is 160 GWh/yr by 2030, serving ~2.2M EVs. The Polish government committed €350M in grants on a total €1.7B investment. As of mid-2026, no confirmed announcement of delay or cancellation has been found, but PowerCo's Salzgitter gigafactory demand was already being met from Umicore's existing Nysa capacity.

companies.name: EcoPro
companies.notes: EcoPro BM — South Korean cathode material company with European plant in Debrecen.

research.summary: EcoPro BM started commercial CAM production at its Debrecen plant in late 2025 (construction completed, plant inaugurated December 2025). Current capacity is 54,000 t/a high-nickel ternary cathode materials (NCA and NMC) — consistent with the 54,500 t/a in the source image. EcoPro plans to expand to 108,000 t/a in 2026. Total investment was €728M; ~600 jobs created. The plant supplies Samsung SDI, with a reported $34B long-term supply agreement.

open_questions: Building reportedly ready Q1 2025 — monitor equipment installation and Phase 1 (50,000 t/a) production start

research.summary: Huayou Cobalt (China) began construction of its first European CAM plant in Ács, Hungary in June 2024 (piling and columns underway by end-2024). Plant building (116,000 m²) targeted for occupation Q1 2025. Full capacity 100,000 t/a NMC; Phase 1 at 50,000 t/a. ~€1.4B total investment, ~900 jobs. Likely in equipment installation/commissioning phase as of mid-2026.

research.summary: Italmatch Chemicals (Arese, near Milan) participates in the IPCEI Batteries European project as Europe's sole producer of Phosphorus Pentachloride (PCl5), a precursor for LiPF6 battery electrolyte. Operates a pilot electrolyte precursor plant in Arese (~12 t/a, R&D/demonstration scale). Part of a European effort to establish domestic LiPF6 production capacity.
